_comment: More invented feeds for the Google Play screenshots and video (scripts/play-shots.mjs), added to feeds.json's: a news site, a travel site and a blog, so the phone's Feeds show the kinds of feeds people follow. Sites and authors are made up; `picture` is a file of scripts/shots/previews.

posts.author: Elena Marsh
posts.title: Cities switch their street lights to warmer, dimmer nights
posts.excerpt: A dozen cities are trading bright white street lights for warmer, dimmer ones after midnight, and residents say they sleep better.
body: A dozen cities are trading bright white street lights for warmer, dimmer ones after midnight, and residents say they sleep better.
The change costs little: most new lamps can be dimmed from a central system, and the warmer colour scatters less light into bedrooms and the night sky.
Councils report energy savings of around a third, with no rise in accidents on the streets that changed first.

posts.author: Tom Avery
posts.title: A small satellite will map river floods every six hours
posts.excerpt: A satellite the size of a suitcase is set to send flood maps four times a day, fast enough for towns downstream to prepare.
body: A satellite the size of a suitcase is set to send flood maps four times a day, fast enough for towns downstream to prepare.
Its radar sees through cloud, which is exactly when floods happen and when ordinary pictures from orbit show nothing useful.

posts.author: Inés Calder
posts.title: Three days on foot along the old salt road
posts.excerpt: The salt road crosses two valleys and one pass, and you can still walk it in three easy days with a light pack.
body: The salt road crosses two valleys and one pass, and you can still walk it in three easy days with a light pack.
Villages sit a day apart, each with a guesthouse that will dry your boots and feed you more than you planned to eat.
Go in early autumn: the pass is clear of snow, the days are still long, and the crowds have gone home.

posts.author: Inés Calder
posts.title: Why the best coastal towns are worth visiting in fog
posts.excerpt: Fog empties the promenades and fills the cafés, and a coastal town shows a side of itself the summer never does.
body: Fog empties the promenades and fills the cafés, and a coastal town shows a side of itself the summer never does.
Bring a warm layer, walk the harbour at dawn, and listen for the foghorn: it carries further than you would think.

posts.author: Anna Weller
posts.title: Keeping a reading journal without making it a chore
posts.excerpt: Two lines per book is enough: what it was about, and the one thing you want to remember from it.
body: Two lines per book is enough: what it was about, and the one thing you want to remember from it.
A journal that asks for more gets abandoned by March. One that asks for two lines is still going in December, and those lines add up to a year of reading you can look back on.

posts.author: Anna Weller
posts.title: Notes in the margin, and why paper still wins for them
posts.excerpt: A pencil note in a margin sits exactly where the thought started, which is why so many of us still read with one in hand.
body: A pencil note in a margin sits exactly where the thought started, which is why so many of us still read with one in hand.
Digital highlights are easier to search, but harder to stumble on again. The best system may simply be both.
